title: The Shadow and the Thief

full_text:
Following the burglary of their ashram, Guru Paramartha issued a strict decree that his disciples must maintain night vigils to protect their remaining property. Each disciple was assigned a two-hour watch on the veranda, armed with a heavy bamboo staff.

One moonlit midnight, it was Peedan's turn to stand sentry. The moon was high and bright, casting long, dark, distinct shadows across the whitewashed courtyard wall.

As Peedan marched back and forth, he suddenly noticed a tall, dark, sinister figure with a long staff mimicking his every movement along the wall! When Peedan stepped forward, the dark figure stepped forward; when Peedan raised his stick, the figure raised its stick; and when Peedan stopped, the intruder stopped!

Peedan's teeth began to chatter with terror: 'A thief! A giant demon thief has entered the courtyard and mocks my martial stance!'

Instead of raising an alarm, Peedan decided to reason with the intruder: 'Halt, shadow thief! Who are you, and what is your business in Guru Paramartha's ashram?'

The shadow, naturally, remained completely silent.

'Insolent scoundrel!' whispered Peedan. 'You refuse to answer? Take this!'

Peedan swung his heavy bamboo staff with all his might at the dark figure on the wall! The stout bamboo struck the solid brickwork of the courtyard wall with a bone-jarring crash. The staff splintered into pieces, and the violent rebound sent sharp vibrations through Peedan's wrists, nearly dislocating his thumbs!

Peedan dropped to his knees, clutching his bruised hands, whimpering in pain: 'The thief possesses armor of solid iron! He has broken my weapon without moving a muscle!'

Hearing the crash, Matti and Madayan rushed onto the veranda: 'What has happened, Peedan?'

'Behold the demon thief!' pointed Peedan, trembling. 'He stands against the wall, armed and silent! I struck him with my staff, and his body is hard as granite!'

Madayan examined the wall. As the three disciples moved together, three dark, joined shadows stretched across the whitewash.

Madayan gasped in horror: 'By the gods! He was alone a moment ago, and now he has summoned two ferocious accomplices! They are an army of darkness! We must perform a strategic retreat!'

The three sentries turned and fled into the Guru's bedchamber, diving beneath the Master's cot, trembling and shivering under the blankets.

When dawn broke and the sun rose, the shadows faded away. Guru Paramartha emerged onto the veranda and inspected the splintered staff and the empty courtyard.

Hearing the disciples' terrified account of the three granite-bodied demons, the Guru stroked his beard and delivered his verdict: 'The demons of the night, my children, were dissolved by the sacred power of our morning prayers! But to ensure they never return, we shall whitewash the entire courtyard with lime, for demons are notoriously allergic to fresh paint!'

And for three days, the disciples painted the walls, proud of their glorious victory over the phantom intruders.
moral: He who fights phantoms and fears his own shadow is defeated before the battle begins.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Shadow and the Thief"?
options: Foolishness of book knowledge without worldly wisdom
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
